answer_1.quote: Our proposed attack, RedHerring, is a word-level attacks. It differs from previous research as it focuses on tricking the detector while keeping the classifier correct, while previous research focuses on tricking the classifier.
answer_1.outputs: Modified texts generated by inserting words using BERT-based infilling to trigger attack detectors without changing classifier predictions.

answer_2.quote: We also verify RedHerring's strength by testing it against the T5 generative model ... We measure the semantic integrity of the generated text via BERTScore .

answer_4.quote: To further gauge the effectiveness of RedHerring, we employ 3 human annotators to label texts. The annotators are given the text, the classifier label, We find that RedHerring is indeed able to create a larger disagreement and lack of trust with the detector.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to label 5 sample texts to make sure they understood the instructions. If any were labeled wrong, they were given explanations before being asked to label the full set of texts. Each annotator labeled 120 texts total and were compensated 20 USD for their time.
